chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Abu Ismail, from Abu al-Fadl al-Makfouf (the author of Al-Arabiyya), from Abu Ja'far al-Ahowl al-Taqi, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He was asked about a male slave who marries a free woman, what is the status of the child? He said: 'Free.' I said, 'And if a free man marries a slave woman?' He said: 'The child is attached to the free status, wherever it is. If the mother is free, he is freed with his mother, and if the father is free, he is freed with his father.'
ai.seo_question: What is the legal status of a child born to a slave father and a free mother in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the juristic principle of 'al-waladu li-l-furash' (the child follows the free parent) in mixed-status unions, ensuring the child's emancipation by linking their status to whichever parent is free. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on social mobility and the removal of hereditary servitude, distinguishing it from other schools that may prioritize the father's status. The narration underscores the practical implication that the child is freed through the lineage of the free parent, whether mother or father.
